characterization_methods.technique: Instrumented Charpy impact test (dynamic fracture toughness)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Fatigue precracked Charpy specimens; Schindler single-specimen technique
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Schindler method per ASTM E 1820 and ASTM E 813
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure dynamic fracture toughness (DFT) of quenched and tempered cast 4130 benchmark for correlation with Fe-Mn-Al-C lightweight steels
characterization_methods.key_findings: Cast 4130 quenched and tempered: DFT 94 kJ/m² at 350 BHN and DFT 136 kJ/m² at 330 BHN

unmapped_findings: Cast 4130 (quenched and tempered) serves as the benchmark alloy for strength and dynamic fracture toughness comparison with the Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.9C lightweight steels.
The fully austenitic Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.9C cast steels are almost 15% less dense than quenched and tempered Cr-Mo steels (SAE 4130) with equivalent strengths and dynamic fracture toughness.
Porosity in high-strength steel was reported to decrease the toughness of quenched and tempered Cr and Mo steel by more than 50 kJ/m².
The composition of the SAE 4130 benchmark is not reported in the paper; Table IV identifies it only as 'Cast 4130' with heat treatment 'Quenched and tempered'.
